subject: RE: Intermittent request stalls — request-pattern fingerprinting & exec sync
messages:
From: Rachel Shaw <rachel@cartflux.io>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: ops@cartflux.io
Date: Fri, 01 Sep 2028 17:22:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent request stalls and p99 degradation (Cartflux production)

Laura —

We started seeing a recurring pattern in Cartflux production over the last 18 hours: a cluster of requests (roughly 0.6% of traffic) experience >10s stalled completions and some 504s. P99 has climbed from 420ms to ~9.8s during the windows; throughput overall steady. No recent deploy on our side.

Attached is a telemetry snapshot (telemetry_snapshot_20280901.csv) with request ids and timestamps, plus a short sample trace (sample_trace.txt). Key observations:
- Spikes are tightly clustered in 2–3 minute windows, recurring every ~30–45 mins.
- Affected requests show long queue wait times before any runtime CPU/GPU utilization rise.
- Error rate for that micro-batch shows retries and occasional 5xx.

This is user-impacting for a subset of flows. We need a quick root-cause signal and an estimate for mitigation (temporary routing or throttles) before our execs escalate. Are you able to triage?

Thanks,
Rachel Shaw
SRE — Cartflux
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Rachel Shaw <rachel@cartflux.io>
Date: Fri, 01 Sep 2028 17:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Intermittent request stalls and p99 degradation (Cartflux production)

Team —

Acknowledged. Rachel, thanks for the quick data — helpful pattern.

Immediate asks: can someone take lead on a fast assessment (30–45 minute run) to surface whether this is queueing/backpressure at the edge, KV-cache saturation, or a recent runtime scheduling change? Marcus — can you pull aggregated queue_length and pending-worker histograms aligned to the windows Rachel flagged? Dev — look for recent runtime kernel/priority scheduling changes and whether concurrency caps recently applied to Cartflux tenant. Tessa — coordinate the exec call if we need to escalate (I want an exec sync if we can’t get a mitigation in 60 minutes).

Proposed immediate mitigations to consider (we can pick after quick triage):
- Emergency route to a larger Dedicated pool (if capacity available)
- Short window increase of concurrency cap for Cartflux (controlled bump)
- Enable stricter prefix caching for repeated prompt patterns

I’m attaching our mitigation_playbook_v2.pdf for reference. Marcus/Dev — please post telemetry snippets to the Jira SRV-1123 and share the Drive link.

I’ll schedule a 30-minute exec call for 18:30 PT if we need one; hold until I confirm.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Rachel Shaw <rachel@cartflux.io>
Date: Fri, 01 Sep 2028 18:16:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Intermittent request stalls and p99 degradation (Cartflux production)

Quick update from my side after a 20-min dive: hypothesis = transient KV-cache pressure + enforced tenant concurrency cap interaction. Details:
- The runtime change we shipped this morning (scheduler tweak to reduce worker preemption) introduced a heavier tail for queued requests when many short-lived requests hit the same KV partitions.
- Cartflux patterns show repeated small payloads with identical prefixes (likely personalization lookups) — this amplifies KV hotness and increases lock contention in the prefix cache path.
- Concurrency cap for Cartflux was lowered as part of quota adjustments yesterday (cap=160). When small bursts line up with cache hotness, queue length climbs and preemption change means queued requests wait instead of stealing workers.

Immediate mitigations I can enact now (risk/rollback noted):
1) Temporarily increase Cartflux concurrency cap to 260 — low risk, short duration (rollback in 30 mins)
2) Enable sticky prefix caching for their tenant for the next 2 hours (should reduce KV hits by ~30%)
3) If available, fail traffic to a Dedicated pool (larger instance classes) — needs ops approval.

I’ll prepare a quick config diff and a rollback command set. Marcus — can you validate queue histograms vs. cap thresholds?

—Dev
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Rachel Shaw <rachel@cartflux.io>
Date: Fri, 01 Sep 2028 18:44:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Intermittent request stalls and p99 degradation (Cartflux production)

Logs & quick telemetry attached (runtime_metrics_20280901.json). Short notes from my analysis:
- Aligned the queue_length histogram to the windows Rachel flagged: 95th–99.5th percentile queue wait climbs dramatically in the 2–3 minute windows she described.
- Worker-utilization stays relatively flat during spikes — consistent with queueing at admission rather than execution fatigue.
- Peaks line up with a small set (~0.5%) of request hashes hitting the same prefix groups.

Recommendation path:
A) Short-term: Approve Dev’s concurrency cap bump + enable sticky prefix caching. That should collapse the queue tail within one burst window.
B) Mid-term (next 72 hours): Rollback the scheduler tweak to previous preemption defaults for a canary set while we test a more nuanced backpressure policy that accounts for KV hotness.
C) Ops: If Cartflux approves, move critical traffic to a Dedicated pool for 1–2 hours while we validate.

Filed telemetry and notes in SRV-1123; drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cExampleSharedTelemetry.

—Marcus
Staff SRE — Redwood Inference

Date: Sat, 02 Sep 2028 06:05:00 -0700
Subject: Cartflux mitigation plan & exec sync (proposed)

Rachel — quick update and ask for permission to proceed with short-term mitigations. We’ve completed a rapid triage and believe the root cause signal is queueing induced by KV-cache hotness interacting with a recent scheduler preemption change + a conservative concurrency cap for your tenant. Proposed immediate actions (will take effect within ~8–12 minutes once approved):
1) Increase Cartflux concurrency cap from 160 -> 260 (auto-rollback after 30 minutes)
2) Enable sticky prefix caching for Cartflux for 2 hours
3) Standby: if latency does not improve within one burst window, fail ~20% of traffic to a Dedicated pool (no code change; routing only).

We’re scheduled for a 30-minute exec sync at 18:30 PT today (call details: Zoom ID: 987-654-321). I’ll invite Redwood ops and our infra exec on the call if you want exec-level context. Please either reply with GO or call ops@redwood with authorization.

Also: to address your compliance note — all failover routing will remain in-region (us-west) and KMS keys stay customer-bound; we will not snapshot customer data into external buckets.

If I don’t hear back by 18:20 PT we’ll proceed with the concurrency bump + prefix caching as a conservative mitigation and hold on the Dedicated failover until explicit GO.

Best,
Laura
